(p-225) SURAH AL-TAKATHUR (The Race for More)

Its purpose is to state explicitly what Surah al-'Adiyat (The Chargers) alluded to: that the cause of ruin on the Day of Gathering, whose form is al-Qari'ah (The Striking Calamity), is the gathering of wealth and the inclination toward the abode of passing away. Its name is clearly indicative of this. "In the name of Allah," Possessor of Majesty and Honour, "the Most Gracious" who encompassed all with bounty, [by clarification -] after accusation, and bringing into existence after annihilation, "the Most Merciful" who singled out His loved ones with the perfect continuation of His blessing.

* *

When [Allah] established in al-Qari'ah the matter of the Hour, divided people in it into wretched and happy, and concluded with the wretched, He opened this surah with the cause of wretchedness and the origin of the gathering, so that the listener would be restrained from this cause and be among the first category. He said, in summary: You have divided, and a group among you became lost, because ﴿your preoccupation diverted you﴾, that is, it made you heedless, with a great heedlessness, except for the rare few among you, of death, which alone is sufficient to drive one to asceticism, let alone what comes after it. ﴿The race for more﴾ is boasting and vying in the multiplication of perishable accidents of worldly goods: wealth, rank, children, and the like, which distract from God. This necessarily directs the entire aspiration toward accumulation, and so it diverted you into frivolity, and it made you heedless (p-226) of what lies before you of the Hereafter and the true religion, of the remembrance of your Lord, and of everything that would save you from His wrath. Or it made you heedless of competing in the deeds that lead to the highest ranks through abundance of acts of obedience. All of this is because you do not submit to what has overcome you of ignorance, whose cause is the desire of the soul and the love of ease, so your scales have become light. He omitted the object of this heedlessness to magnify it and to indicate that there is nothing else which would be regretted as a diversion from it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 102, verse 2:

Since they denied the resurrection and believed in the lasting of dwelling in the graves, [He] expressed it with "visiting" (ziyarah), as an indication that the resurrection is unavoidable and that there is no doubt about it, and that the tarrying in the barzakh, however long it lasts, is only like the tarrying of a visitor with the one he visits, compared with the dwelling after the resurrection in the abode of bliss or the cave of Hellfire. And [it indicates] that dwelling [in the grave] is loved, because of the knowledge of what comes after it of terrors, hardships and frights. So He said: ﴿Until﴾, meaning: your boasting and your competing in abundance continued until ﴿you visited the graves﴾, meaning, by death and burial, so that you were in them exposed to the resurrection, unable to do what would save you, because the abode of action has passed away, just as the visitor is not in a position of knowledge with the one visited. They do not remain in them except for a little while until those who are gathered by death are complete, just as the visitor is liable to return to his home and his final residence. So if the only thing preventing you from turning to this world were death, it would have been sufficient; how much more so when the matter is greater than that? For death is an introduction to the preliminaries of the Reckoning. Abu Hayyan said: Some Bedouin heard the verse and said: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, the resurrection of the people is for the Final Day!" For the visitor is one who departs, not one who remains. And Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz that he recited it and then said: "I see the graves only as a visit, and whoever visits must return to his house, either to Paradise or to the Fire."

And Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When the mention of the Striking Calamity (al-qari'ah) and its great terrors had preceded, He followed it with mention of what occupies and turns one away from preparing for it and distracts from remembering it, namely competition in number, relatives and kin. So He said: ﴿Competition in abundance has diverted you﴾ [al-Takathur: 1], and it is in the context of threat and reproof. It was followed by what reinforces this, namely His saying ﴿Nay, you will soon know﴾ [al-Takathur: 3], ﴿Then nay, you will soon know﴾ [al-Takathur: 4], then He said: ﴿Nay, if you knew with certain knowledge﴾ [al-Takathur: 5]. The answer to "law" (law) is omitted, and the estimate is: "If you knew with certain knowledge, competition in abundance would not have occupied you." He ﷺ said:

"If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much," the hadith.

And His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, you will surely see the Hellfire﴾ is the answer to an implied oath, meaning: By Allah, you will surely see the Hellfire; the threat is thereby emphasized, and likewise what follows to the end of the surah. Ended.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 102, verse 3:

Since preoccupation with multiplying (al-takathur) is a clear sign of foolishness, for it is certainly known that this existence in this order cannot be except by a wise Maker, and since rational people who benefit from existence are extremely unjust toward one another, and since the Wise would never at all accept that His servants wrong one another without judging between them or attending to their interests, it is certainly known that He will raise them up to judge between them, because just as He was able to originate them, He is able to bring them back. He has promised this, sent His messengers with it, and revealed His books with it. Thus it is established with an established certainty that admits no doubt and no addition. The situation calls for the strongest deterrence against those who turn away from what concerns them and occupy themselves with what does not concern them. So He, glorified is He, expressed it with the mother of deterrents and the comprehensive of restraints and warnings: ﴿Nay﴾, that is, be restrained with the fullest restraint and be stopped with the greatest prohibition from preoccupation with what yields no benefit. For the matter is not as you suppose, that boasting in multiplication through worldly accidents is what counts, and you were not created for that. Rather, you were created for a great matter, and it is that which should concern you [so you occupied yourselves with what does not concern you -], and so you became heedless, like one for whom a dirham each day suffices but who busies himself with acquiring more. Likewise is one who neglects the essential part of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) and occupies himself with weak opinions (al-aqwal al-shadhdhah), or neglects the essential part of fiqh (jurisprudence) and occupies himself with rare subsidiary cases (nawadir al-furu') and the causes of grammar (ilal al-nahw) and other things, and neglects (p-229) what is more important than these, that on which his life depends.

Since deterrence is only from something harmful that brings ruin and regret, He indicated this by His saying, as a resumption: ﴿Soon﴾, that is, after a long respite in which whoever takes heed will take heed, ﴿you will know﴾, that is, there will be renewed for you knowledge, by a promise that admits no failure, of the error you are upon, at the moment of witnessing what death will uncover, and what the loss of opportunity will bring in grief, of its consequence and its ruin.

Since some matters are such that, were their description given as they truly are, it would run long and lead to tedium, he indicated that the explanation of this threat is awesome, by his words—emphasizing it, along with the use of the particle of delay that indicates the loftiness of the rank: ﴿Then, no!﴾ That is, be restrained with a restraint greater than that, because ﴿you will come to know﴾, that is, knowledge will come to you without doubt, even if its time is delayed a little, by the Resurrection.

When this was a decisive matter, he indicated that it is sufficient for this merciful community to be emphasized once. So he repeated the matter, placing among the two emphases of deterrence a third, using the particle suited to both and to the meaning, truly, as the imams of qira'ah (recitation) say: ﴿Kalla﴾ [i.e.,] so that their restraint from excessive accumulation (al-takathur) may be intensified, for it is the foundation of every calamity. Then ﴿if you knew﴾, O you who accumulate.

Since knowledge (al-'ilm) may be applied to supposition (al-zann), its figurative sense was removed by his saying ﴿the knowledge of certainty﴾, meaning: if knowledge of the form of certainty (al-yaqin) were to occur to you (p-230) even once in your lifetime, you would know what lies before you. Then distraction by accumulation would not have diverted you, you would have laughed little and wept much, and you would have gone out to the open places, crying out. He omitted this response after omitting the object, for the sake of magnifying the matter. This indicates that there is no certainty other than it, and the meaning is that your deeds are the deeds of one who does not have certainty of it.

Al-Razi said: Yaqin (certainty) is a compound of taking in this path, and it is the ultimate degree of the common people and the first step of the elite. The prayer and peace of Allah be upon him said: "The best thing cast into the heart is certainty." And it is the knowledge of accepting what has become manifest of the truth, accepting what is hidden for the truth, and standing upon what has been established by the truth.

The verse is an instance of al-ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which a paired element is omitted from each of two parts, each omission being supplied by the other): he mentioned distraction first and omitted its cause, which is ignorance, because the second part indicates it. Second, he mentioned knowledge, which is the fruit, and omitted what results from it of the absence of distraction, which is the opposite of the first. He also increased the magnification of this threat by clarifying what is threatened after leaving it vague, together with an oath indicated by its lam, so he said:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 102, verse 6:

﴿Certainly you will see﴾ i.e., with direct witnessing (al-mukashafah), by Our might. It is not correct for this to be the answer (jawab) to what precedes it, because that is already certain. ﴿the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim)﴾ i.e., the Fire into which the tormented are cast with loathing, fury and fierce intensity of blaze. The believer will see it and be saved from it, whether or not he passes through it, while the disbeliever will abide in it forever.

Since this is a warning against worldly rivalry in abundance, for it entails turning away from the Hereafter and so falls into the great calamities, He emphasized it, magnifying it with the particle of delay (thumma), saying: ﴿Then you will surely see it﴾. The might of God and the elevation of knowledge are beyond the rank of the first alone, so He said, exalted is He: ﴿with the certainty of sight﴾, that is, the sight which is itself certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn), and this is direct witnessing, with the utmost purity of knowledge, since there is no doubt in it, for witnessing is the highest kind of knowledge. Al-Rāzī said: it is what dispenses, through immediate apprehension, with inference (istidlāl), and with report through direct seeing, and when witnessing tears away the veil of knowledge. End of quotation. It is also possible that this second [sight] is by contact and entering, so the believer comes to it and the disbeliever abides in it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 102, verse 8:

Since the most fearsome form of address is the threat of seeing the punishment, He increased the warning by stating that the punishment with which the disobedient one is tormented is made ready (ʿatīd), so that when questioning brings about chastisement, it is present, with nothing preventing its being inflicted immediately. If it were not present, then for the one who deserves it, its being brought forth within the time of its bringing would be impossible. So He said, magnifying it by using the particle of delay: ﴿Then﴾, meaning after long, great and extremely awesome matters, ﴿you will surely be questioned﴾, by Our might, ﴿that Day﴾, meaning when you see the Blazing Fire, ﴿about the bliss﴾, meaning that which the competition for worldly gain brought you to, to the extent of [being questioned] about cold water in summer and warm [drink] in winter: was your enjoyment of it in a wasteful manner, seeking luxury, or was it for the sake of strength to rise toward good, so that it did not go beyond excess? The believer who obeys is questioned with a question of honour, while the disobedient one is questioned with a question of rebuke and reproach. The lam of "al-naʿīm" may be for the mere genus, and to this points the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, in al-Tirmidhi and others, that the Prophet ﷺ was the guest of Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan together with Abu Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and he fed them dates (busr and rutab) and gave them cold water to drink and spread for them a carpet in the shade. The Prophet ﷺ said:

"Indeed this is among the bliss about which you will be questioned: cool shade, fresh good dates, and cold water."

It may also be for perfection, and then it is among the signs of prophethood, as in the hadith of Mahmud ibn Labid, may Allah be pleased with him, in Ahmad through a good chain: when it was revealed, they said, "What bliss? We have only the two black things: dates and water, while our swords are on our necks and the enemy is present." He said: "Indeed that will come to pass." It has a witness in al-Tabarani from Ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both, and in al-Tabarani also from al-Hasan al-Basri as a mursal report. Thus its end is joined to its beginning in a manner that is among the most subtle address and the most refined paths in forbidding what leads to punishment, for the intelligent person, when he knows that before him is a questioning about everything in which he takes pleasure, knows that this prevents him, at the time of questioning, from the enjoyments of the lofty and precious Garden. So his fear of questioning in general prevents him from indulging in what is permissible, so how about what is disliked, and how much more so what is forbidden? And how if the questioner is an angel before whose awe mountains melt? And how if the questioning is in the manner of reproach? And how if it leads to punishment? So reflect upon the speech of your Creator: how subtle are its allusions and how exalted its expressions, in its warnings and its glad tidings. And Allah is most merciful.
